universities.name: Anglia Ruskin University
universities.summary: Anglia Ruskin University is a public university with a School of Medicine in Chelmsford. Its five-year MBChB Medicine degree is approved by the General Medical Council and combines campus teaching with patient-care learning across hospitals, GP surgeries and community settings from Year 1.
universities.campusLifestyle: MBChB students are based at ARU’s School of Medicine in Chelmsford. The official course page lists skills laboratories, GP simulation rooms, a Category 2 SuperLab and an Anatomy Centre with dissection, embalming, radiology, virtual-dissection and ultrasound facilities.
universities.cityProfile: Chelmsford is the location for ARU’s five-year MBChB. The course page does not give one universal student-living budget, but identifies accommodation, bills, travel, food, study materials and social costs as separate planning items. Placement travel is an additional medicine-course cost and varies by placement.
universities.practicalExposure: ARU states that Medicine students gain hands-on patient-care experience from Year 1 and complete placements in all five years. The published model includes hospitals, GP surgeries and community settings, with skills laboratories, GP simulation rooms and anatomy facilities supporting campus-based preparation; it is a clinical-learning structure, not an employment guarantee.
universities.hostelOverview: ARU’s Medicine page identifies accommodation as a living-cost component but does not publish a Medicine-specific accommodation rate or guarantee a room. Applicants should plan accommodation separately from the published UK tuition charge and allow for travel to clinical placements.
universities.dietarySupport: ARU does not publish a compulsory Medicine meal-plan cost on the course page. Food and drink are listed as part of individual living costs, separate from tuition and additional course costs, so the admissions cost plan should not treat tuition as a complete annual budget.
universities.safetyOverview: Medicine offers are conditional on satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service and Occupational Health checks. ARU does not publish campus-specific safety statistics on the course page; the disclosed professional checks are relevant to suitability for clinical learning rather than a general safety rating.
universities.studentSupport: The Medicine selection route includes UCAT, UCAS, academic screening, ranking and Multiple Mini Interviews. ARU’s course team, healthcare professionals, junior doctors and service users participate in selection, while accepted applicants complete DBS and Occupational Health requirements before joining clinical learning.

faq.question: Can international-fee students apply for ARU Medicine?
faq.answer: No. ARU’s current MBChB page states that applicants must have home fee status at the point of application. This is a material eligibility restriction, not simply a fee difference.

faq.question: How long is the ARU Medicine degree?
faq.answer: The MBChB runs for five years and starts in September in Chelmsford. ARU states that placements run across all five years.

faq.question: Is the MBChB approved by the GMC?
faq.answer: Yes. ARU states that its MBChB Medicine degree is approved by the General Medical Council after the GMC quality-assurance process. This supports the UK course’s regulatory status but does not guarantee registration in another jurisdiction.

faq.question: What are the main academic requirements?
faq.answer: For standard A-level entry, ARU lists AAA including Chemistry or Biology and one of Biology, Chemistry, Maths, Physics or Psychology, plus specified GCSE requirements. The course page also lists IB, T Level, graduate and other routes with their own conditions.

faq.question: What UCAT and interview steps apply?
faq.answer: Applicants take UCAT, apply through UCAS by the medicine deadline, pass ARU’s academic screen and are ranked for shortlisting. Shortlisted candidates complete Multiple Mini Interviews; offers then remain conditional on the stated checks.

faq.question: What is the 2026/27 tuition fee?
faq.answer: ARU lists GBP 9,790 per year for UK students starting in 2026/27. The course is self-funded for the standard tuition years; placement travel, DBS, a stethoscope and books are additional costs.

admissionsContent.overview: ARU Medicine is a home-fee-status-only, restricted-entry MBChB. The route uses UCAT, a complete UCAS application, academic screening, UCAT ranking and Multiple Mini Interviews; students should establish fee eligibility before investing in test and application preparation.

eligibility.intro: The course page sets academic, UCAT, fee-status and professional-suitability requirements, with different published routes for A levels, IB, T Levels and graduates.
items: Home fee status at point of application
AAA at A level for standard entry, including Chemistry or Biology and one specified science-related subject
Minimum four GCSEs at grade 5/B or above including Maths, English Language and two sciences
IELTS 7.5 overall with 7.0 in each component for applicants requiring English evidence
Satisfactory DBS and Occupational Health checks after offer

applicationSteps: Register for and take UCAT in the published testing window
Prepare and submit the UCAS Medicine application by 15 October
Complete ARU’s WAMS questionnaire if sent and relevant
Pass academic screening and UCAT-based shortlisting
Attend Multiple Mini Interviews if shortlisted
Meet offer, DBS and Occupational Health conditions before enrollment

academic: GCSE and A-level, IB, T Level or equivalent evidence
application: DBS and Occupational Health documentation after offer

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: ARU states that Medicine applications open in September before entry and close on 15 October each year. UCAT registration runs May–September and testing runs from early July to early October.

programmes.feeNotes: GBP 9,790 per year is the published 2026/27 UK-student fee. The programme requires home fee status, and course-specific costs include variable placement travel, DBS, a stethoscope and books.

evidence.claimText: Anglia Ruskin University delivers its MBChB Medicine course through its School of Medicine in Chelmsford.
ARU states that its MBChB Medicine degree is approved by the General Medical Council after a quality-assurance process.
ARU requires home fee status at point of application and publishes academic, UCAT, English and professional-suitability requirements for MBChB Medicine.
The ARU selection route requires UCAT, UCAS application, academic screening, UCAT ranking and Multiple Mini Interviews, followed by conditional DBS and Occupational Health requirements.
The MBChB starts in September, and ARU states that UCAS Medicine applications close on 15 October each year.
